_comment: Counted-metrics ledger, family 'copies' (#2137). Pins are MEASURED (WIDE) or a STATIC count read from the code (MID), never round ceilings. Re-pin only by a deliberate PR edit: python3 bench/counted_ledger.py pins --raw <bench_peer_counts transcript> --write.
title: User-space copies per relayed frame
_toolchain: Copy and syscall counts follow the code, but which copies the compiler inlines does not, so a run on another toolchain is reported in warn mode and never turns CI red.
_band: 0: a copy count is exact. Every pinned row read min = max over 3 repetitions, and its median matched the peer-cost study's TCP figures byte for byte. The WS rows read lower than the study's (3150 against 3266 B at 1 KiB) because this run is paced, so the stream buffer never holds a second frame's tail when it compacts.
_goal: From #2136: ingress receives straight into an exact-length segment (0 copies), a server egress is one shared frame (0), a WS client send gathers and masks in one pass (1x), the 48 B TCP client handoff head stays. The copy-or-share trait (#2143) removed the stored-value copy wherever the receive segment fits the value's size class. UDP ingress already receives into a max_frame segment (#2136 ingress), and on the slab pool a value whose size class is smaller than that segment's is copied out of it (RFC-0022 Am.3), so a UDP-in relay row at 4 and 16 KiB carries that copy under a waiver until #2142 (right-sized UDP receive segment) lands and restores the share.

rows.moved_by: #2171 (first pin)
rows.basis: esp_ws_client_link.cpp send: gather_into copies every span of the frame once, into the tx_ slot when another send is writing or into tx_buf_ when this one writes (1). esp_transport_write then masks the buffer in place and unmasks it after the write: two XOR passes, no copy. Payload bytes only, as the other MID rows count them; the frame's FWD envelope is copied with it. The lwIP pbuf copy is the stack's, like the kernel's on WIDE. Goal from #2136 user story 16: gather and mask in one pass, so the copy stays and the two passes go.
